the emergence of drug‐resistance mutations was similar in the ZDV group and non‐TA group, and the rate of emergence of drug‐ resistance mutations was similar between groups.

the emergence of drug‐resistance mutations differed in patients failing first line antiretrovial therapy (ART) regimens containing one NNRIT administered with ZDV + lamivudines (ZDV group) compared with those administered without thymidine analogue (non‐TAS; non‐TA group), with a higher frequency of mutations associated with resistance to ZDV in the non‐TA groups.

the study of drug resistance in HIV‐1‐positive patients failing first‐lined antiretrovial therapy containing non‐nucleoside analogues with and without thimidine analogue.
the development of drug resistance in the two groups of patients.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ZDV group showed a significantly lower proportion of NNRTI‐resistant viruses than the non‐TA one.
the NNRTIs are not associated with a higher risk of developing drug‐resistance mutations than the non‐NRTI class.
there is no evidence of a difference in resistance patterns between the two groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NNRTI‐based regimens containing a thymidine analogue (ZDV) were associated with a higher frequency of drug resistance mutations (DRMs) at failure than those containing a non‐TA.
NNRTI‐resistant virus is more common in the ZDV group, whereas thymidine analog resistance is more common in those receiving non‐TAs.
NNRTI resistance mutations emerged more frequently in the ZDV group than in the non‐TA one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of resistance differs between patients failing first‐ line antiretrovial therapy containing nonnucleside reverse transcriptase with or without thymidine analogue.
patients failing NNRTI‐based regimens containing ZDV have a higher probability of developing resistance to ZDV than those failing regimens containing non‐TAs.
patients with a history of ZDV‐based first‐line treatment are more prone to develop NNRTI‐associated resistance than those with a history of non‐TAs, regardless of the NNRTI used.
